title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — otherwise four-term syllogism; conclusion omnes = persons distinct from Adam
pass_a_gloss: Else Paul's argument is a four-term fallacy. Schematized: whoever sinned, death entered them; all sinned; so death entered all. The conclusion's 'all' means persons distinct from Adam—so the minor's 'all' must mean those same distinct persons.
pass_b_english: Otherwise the Apostle's syllogism would be faulty and composed of four terms, which you may form thus: Whoever sinned, into them death passed; all sinned; therefore into all death passed. For in the conclusion the word "all" marks the persons of all men, distinct among themselves and from Adam's person. So in the minor the same word must likewise signify the distinct and separate persons of all men, both among themselves and from Adam.
source_text: Alioqui vitiosus esset Apostoli syllogismus, & ex quatuor terminis componeretur, quem sic forms: Quicumque peccaverunt, in eos mors transiit; Omnes peccaverunt; Igitur in omnes mors transiit. Nam in conclusione vox omnes notat personas omnium hominum inter se & a persona Adami distinctas & separatas. Ergo necesse est ut in minore eadem vox omnium itidem hominum personas distinctas & separatas cum inter se tum ab Adamo significet.

choices.choice: Four-term risk; conclusion all = distinct persons
